title: Variance Source Explorer
description: A live histogram of simulated FFT timings with a tight baseline cluster and a one-sided interrupt tail, alongside running mean, standard deviation, and minimum.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Benchmarking
Statistics

learningObjectives: Interpret a histogram of repeated timing measurements
Explain why interrupt interference is right-skewed rather than symmetric
Justify the minimum as an estimator of intrinsic cost

simulationModel.modelType: Mixture distribution: Gaussian baseline plus one-sided outliers
equations: interfered run = clean run + uniform(50, 150) microseconds
assumptions: Interference is strictly additive, never subtractive
Baseline jitter is Gaussian via Box-Muller
limitations: Real interference has structure — periodic timer ticks produce clustered rather than independent outliers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Accumulating live distribution with contrasting robust and non-robust statistics
keyQuestions: Why can the tail only be on the right?
Which statistic estimates the code's intrinsic cost?
commonMisconceptions: That timing variation is symmetric measurement noise
That the mean is always the best summary
assessmentOpportunities: Infer interrupt activity from the presence or absence of a tail
